rows.title: After one alarming tax fairness study, CT is wary of launching a second
rows.standfirst: After a 2014 study found CT’s tax system hammers the poor and middle class, officials have postponed a second analysis.

rows.title: Lamont and tribes deadlock over sports betting
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont endorsed legalizing sports betting under terms opposed by the tribal owners of Foxwoods Resort and Mohegan Sun.

rows.title: Lamont is lenient on spending cap — when it comes to partnership with Dalio
rows.standfirst: For the second time in two years, Lamont wants to keep state’s $20 million contribution outside the spending cap.

rows.title: Slots on your smartphone? Lamont says, ‘No.’
rows.standfirst: Is Connecticut ready to offer casino games on your phone or laptop? Gov. Ned Lamont is not.

rows.title: Hiring of PR firm by Dalio Philanthropies renews concerns about transparency and ‘blurred lines’
rows.standfirst: A PR-firm hired by Dalio Philanthropies to speak for Connecticut’s public-private education partnership prompted new complaints about the lack of transparency.

rows.title: CT budget is poised to weather coronavirus crisis – for now
rows.standfirst: COVID-19 is certain to pose fiscal challenges for Connecticut — but keeping the state’s books in balance in the short term isn’t one of them.

rows.title: Legislators to break Lamont’s ‘debt diet’ by more than $1B
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers are expected to approve a two-year, $4.7 billion bond package Wednesday that shatters the governer’s “debt diet.”

rows.title: CT’s traditional economic sectors at major risk as coronavirus spreads
rows.standfirst: Connecticut’s manufacturing, tourism and hospitality sectors are on the front lines as the coronavirus spreads.

rows.title: Lamont allows towns to hold meetings remotely to limit spread of coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont permitted municipalities to exclude residents from meetings. But can taxpayers still approve a town budget?

rows.title: Tribes agree to close casinos for two weeks
rows.standfirst: As pressure grew, the Mashantucket Pequot and Mohegan tribes agreed Monday night to close their casinos in response to COVID-19.

rows.title: Tong records 71 price-gouging complaints in first week
rows.standfirst: The complaints include one from a resident who was charged nearly $40 for a 30-pack of toilet paper.

rows.title: Unemployment claims skyrocket as coronavirus crisis deepens
rows.standfirst: At least 25,000 people have filed for unemployment since Friday, prompting the Department of Labor to conduct at-home drills.

rows.title: Trump aims to send Americans $1,000 to cope with COVID-19, but Chris Murphy doubles down
rows.standfirst: Murphy is pushing for each man, woman and child to receive at least $2,000.

rows.title: The night COVID-19 silenced the slots at Foxwoods
rows.standfirst: Foxwoods has stayed open for 28 years through blizzards, hurricanes, and the terrorism attack of Sept. 11. Until Tuesday.

rows.title: Wooden: CT’s cash pool is twice as strong as early days of last recession
rows.standfirst: The coronavirus may have stymied Connecticut’s economy, but state government’s cash flow — and therefore it’s ability to respond — remains very strong.

rows.title: Himes: Coronavirus brings ‘the start of a very, very difficult economic period’
rows.standfirst: Himes says the government must rush money to Americans on the “suffering frontier” of the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Providers warn coronavirus is straining Connecticut’s safety net
rows.standfirst: Nonprofit social services are struggling to keep programs open. Closures would leave clients unprotected and would financially doom some agencies.

rows.title: Lamont, governors from region, ask for $100 billion from feds to respond to coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Connecticut, New York, Pennsylvania and New Jersey say they are “on the front lines” of the coronavirus emergency.

rows.title: Lamont orders non-essential businesses to close during public health crisis
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont: “It’s tough medicine. I think it’s the right medicine.”

rows.title: Lamont pushes CT income tax filing deadline back to July 15
rows.standfirst: The move was anticipated given the decision to push the federal income tax filing deadline back to July 15.

rows.title: Lamont empowers town leaders to adopt budgets without going before voters
rows.standfirst: The waiver exempting municipalities from holding town meetings comes as Connecticut reports its fifth death from coronavirus.

rows.title: Lamont defines ‘essential’ businesses that can remain in operation after Monday
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s ban exempts areas like child and health care, food and safety, gun sales and package stores.

rows.title: Congress struggles to pass coronavirus bill as COVID-19 cases grow
rows.standfirst: Blumenthal and Murphy say a stalled Senate bill fails to provide enough money for states, hospitals and individuals.

rows.title: State braces for major surge in COVID-19 cases
rows.standfirst: State health officials now expect Connecticut’s COVID-19 infection rate to double every 3-5 days.

rows.title: Trump wants normalcy. Lamont, Cuomo warn the worst is yet to come
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump told America it will soon be time to go back to work. If only, say the governors.

rows.title: Deal reached on massive coronavirus bill, but hurdles remain
rows.standfirst: The bill would pour billions into states like Connecticut, give Americans $1,200 checks and boost unemployment benefits.

rows.title: Laid off due to COVID-19? The wait for benefits is 3 weeks
rows.standfirst: The COVID-19 effect in Connecticut: The time to process a jobless claim has jumped from three days to three weeks.

rows.title: Coronavirus begins to widen hole in state finances
rows.standfirst: The first sign that the coronavirus has infected Connecticut’s budget presented itself Wednesday.

rows.title: Lamont’s first try at COVID-19 relief: 0% loans for small businesses
rows.standfirst: A plan to help people who have lost their jobs is slated for debut later this week.

rows.title: Senate approves coronavirus stimulus bill that will send billions to Connecticut
rows.standfirst: Lamont said the state would get at least $1.25 billion, but Connecticut residents and businesses will receive money too.

rows.title: Here’s how coronavirus rescue bill boosts unemployment benefits
rows.standfirst: It would give the jobless an additional $600 a week in benefits and allow self-employed people to file claims.

rows.title: House approves massive coronavirus bill
rows.standfirst: DeLauro, Himes, Courtney and Larson all drove from Connecticut to approve $2 trillion package amid coronavirus concerns.

rows.title: Demand overwhelms emergency business relief program — in two days
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont doubled Connecticut’s business relief program — then suspended applications — after demand quadrupled resources in two days.

rows.title: State can’t print money, but it can guide economic rise from pandemic
rows.standfirst: Connecticut can’t print money like Washington, but it has many options to shield its economy from the coronavirus crisis.

rows.title: When will you get that stimulus check and how big will it be?
rows.standfirst: Most will receive $1,200 checks, but those who don’t file taxes or make too much money will be locked out.

rows.title: Stimulus check poses a host of complications for CT’s working poor
rows.standfirst: For some of Connecticut’s poorest households, the federal stimulus check will be delayed, short-changed, or not coming at all.

rows.title: Coronavirus stimulus bill has millions for CT colleges, gives graduates a break, but not loan forgiveness
rows.standfirst: The CARES Act will help colleges with unexpected expenses. But education advocates say it’s not enough.
